As /u/gekkope mentioned, a manual is necessary. If you don't have a particular brand of bullet you like to load, Lee and Lyman both make good generic manuals. However, if you prefer a particular bullet brand, I'd recommend their manual. Personally, I recommend a powder trickler in. Regarding your bullet tray/loading block/whatever you want to call it, I used to use the RCBS universal tray but recently switched to the Frankford Arsenal Perfect Fit Reloading Tray. Although it is more caliber family specific, I find the fit is better.

Once you become more proficient and want to load volume, I'd recommend a powder thrower to speed up your process a little. That'll provide a more gradual step into the eventual progressive press.
